Want to invent a new kind of model? Here: So if you want to invent a new kind of model, here's a map of where people are pushing: each idea changes one part of the engine that TinyGPT runs on.
RoPE rotates queries and keys by their p: RoPE rotates queries and keys by their position, so attention sees relative distance. It helps stretch context, but using very long contexts well is still hard.
Efficient attention approximates or rest: Efficient attention methods approximate or restrict attention, like with sliding windows, to dodge that quadratic cost, which often means losing some quality. FlashAttention, on the other hand, stays exact and just runs faster.
State-space models like Mamba replace at: State-space models like Mamba replace attention with a recurrence that carries a fixed-size state, so the cost grows linearly with length. That leaves an open question: how much exact detail can that state hold?
Grouped-query attention lets several que: Grouped-query attention lets several query heads share one key and value head. That shrinks the KV cache and speeds up generation, usually with little quality loss.
Mixture of experts swaps the MLP for man: Mixture of experts swaps the MLP for many expert MLPs, and a router picks just a few of them per token. That gives you more parameters without proportionally more compute, but balancing the experts is the hard part.
Distillation trains a small student on a: Distillation trains a small student on a big teacher's outputs — either its full probabilities or text it generated. And how much skill survives the shrink? That's the open question.
Retrieval-augmented models look things u: Retrieval-augmented models look things up and put relevant documents into the context, so knowledge can stay fresh without retraining, as long as retrieval finds the right text and the model actually uses it.
Diffusion language models drop left-to-r: Diffusion language models drop left-to-right: they start fully masked, and then refine every position over a number of steps. Whether they match autoregressive quality at scale is still an open question.
Test-time compute spends more thinking p: Test-time compute means spending more thinking on each question, either by writing out reasoning steps or by sampling several answers and voting. And some recent models are trained with reinforcement learning to reason longer.
